page: Vultr vcg-a40-8c-40g-16vram is a GPU-accelerated virtual machine featuring a fractional NVIDIA A40 Ampere GPU with 16 GB of dedicated VRAM. The compute layer is powered by an Intel x86_64 processor configured with 8 shared vCPUs across 4 physical cores, running at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz. System memory consists of 40.0 GB of RAM, providing a resource density of 5.0 GB per core. Local storage is supported by a 740 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results indicate strong performance in specialized workloads, particularly in large language model (LLM) inference. For a small 135M model, the instance achieves top-tier prompt processing speeds of 9944.32 tokens per second and text generation speeds of 464.42 tokens per second. For a medium 7B model, it maintains top-tier performance with 3147.67 tokens per second for prompt processing and 107.73 tokens per second for text generation. Standard CPU and memory benchmarks fall within the average tier, with a PassMark CPU score of 14090.9 and a multi-core stress-ng score of 14175.12.

The primary tradeoff of this instance lies in its shared CPU allocation and fractional GPU configuration, which limits access to approximately one-third of a physical NVIDIA A40 GPU. This resource-sharing model provides a cost-effective entry point for GPU-accelerated workloads, offering high VRAM capacity and NVMe storage density without the expense of a dedicated full GPU. Memory bandwidth is moderate, measuring 88.57 GB/sec for large-block reads and 52.63 GB/sec for large-block writes.

This server configuration is highly suited for medium-scale LLM inference, machine learning model prototyping, and data science tasks that require GPU acceleration but do not demand a full dedicated card. The 740 GB NVMe storage and 40.0 GB of RAM also make it viable for database operations, static web serving, and general-purpose applications requiring a balance of compute, memory, and fast local storage.
description: Vultr vcg-a40-8c-40g-16vram is a GPU-accelerated virtual server designed for workloads requiring moderate parallel processing and fast local storage. It features a fractional NVIDIA A40 Ampere GPU with 16 GB of VRAM, paired with 8 shared Intel x86_64 vCPUs, 40.0 GB of RAM, and a 740 GB NVMe SSD. While general CPU and memory benchmarks fall in the average tier, the instance delivers top-tier performance in LLM inference, processing 3147.67 tokens per second for a medium 7B model. The shared CPU allocation and fractional GPU configuration offer a cost-efficient alternative to dedicated GPU instances, making it suitable for machine learning prototyping, data science, and database operations.
